correctness.rationale: The Fourier eigenvalues are four-term cyclotomic sums. Any equality of two eigenvalues yields integer polynomial F vanishing at primitive pth root and at one, forcing F=0 and identical exponent multisets; hence eigenfrequency classes have size d=2 or 4 according to m²≡−1. Detector-coordinate restrictions are minors of prime discrete Fourier matrix, so Chebotarev full-spark theorem gives rank min(r,d) in every spectral class. The Hermitian + absorptive effective generator has strictly negative imaginary eigenvalues off the H-invariant dark subspace, proving bright rank equals eventual capture rank even with Jordan blocks and arbitrary positive rates. In one-sink case the coset Fourier character sum has Σ_classes |Σ_{k∈class}ζ^{kx}|²=p−d for x≠0, giving bright diagonal 1/d. Independently diagonalized small primes p=5,7,13,17 with both resonant and generic m; sampled arbitrary sinks and verified sitewise 1/4 or 1/2, but these checks are finite corroboration only.

final_claim: For prime-order 4-regular circulant graphs with steps ±1,±m (p odd, 2≤m≤(p-1)/2) under identical hopping and positive local absorbers, the absorbing bright dimension for any set of r≥1 sink positions is 1+((p-1)/d) min(r,d), d=4 precisely when m²≡−1 (mod p), otherwise d=2. Full capture for every initial density matrix exactly when r≥d. With one sink, each other vertex has exact eventual capture probability 1/d, independent of site location and rates.
